key_insight: Contrastive multi-modal learning can transfer rich semantic signals from data-rich text to data-poor cybersecurity modalities, reducing shortcut learning and substantially improving out-of-distribution generalization in real-world security tasks.
problem_solved: ML models in cybersecurity often learn superficial shortcuts from lab data and fail in production, especially when some modalities (network telemetry, binaries, logs) are scarce; this work addresses robust cross-modal knowledge transfer to improve real-world performance.
method: Train modality-specific encoders (e.g., text, telemetry, binary features) and align their representations with a contrastive loss so that semantically related samples across modalities are pulled together.

Leverage text as a data-rich anchor: use domain-aware augmentations and hard-negative sampling during contrastive pretraining, then add projection heads and fine-tune on downstream cybersecurity tasks.
Evaluate robustness on cross-environment / OOD splits to demonstrate reduced reliance on shortcuts and improved metrics (F1, recall) in production-like scenarios.
impact: Practitioners can leverage abundant textual signals (reports, logs, labels) to bootstrap reliable models for scarce modalities, improving detection/triage reliability and reducing false alarms when deployed in diverse, real-world environments.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: multiple encoders (text, telemetry, binaries) feeding into a contrastive alignment layer with projection heads.
Embedding visualization (t-SNE/UMAP) comparing pre-alignment vs post-alignment clusters, showing better class separation and modality overlap.
Bar chart or line plot: baseline vs proposed model performance on in-domain and out-of-distribution test sets (F1, recall, precision).
Pipeline flow: pretraining on multimodal pairs → fine-tuning on downstream tasks → deployment with improved OOD robustness (icons for text, network, binary, shield).
paper_title: Improving Generalization on Cybersecurity Tasks with Multi-Modal Contrastive Learning
paper_authors: Jianan Huang, Rodolfo V. Valentim, Luca Vassio, Matteo Boffa, Marco Mellia
